findings.evidence: Lines 86-87 confirm global retry_backoff=True and retry_backoff_max=300. Lines 167-189 show task_annotations only for AI tasks (remove_background, analyze_product_image, generate_angles); no annotations for run_auto_payout_sweep or run_reconciliation_cron.
findings.notes: Finding remains valid. Payout and reconciliation periodic tasks lack per-task rate_limit and concurrency_limit annotations, risking concurrent payout sweeps.

findings.evidence: Lines 244-261 in _startup_background_jobs() show BackupManager IS started: get_backup_manager() is called, a daemon thread runs manager.create_backup() at the configured interval, and a stopper is registered. This is invoked at line 335 via stoppers = _startup_background_jobs().
findings.counter_evidence: Original finding claimed no backup scheduler thread was started in lifespan.py. Current code wires BackupManager into _startup_background_jobs() which is called during app startup.
findings.notes: BackupManager is now properly wired into lifespan startup. The gap described in the audit has been closed.

findings.evidence: Lines 152-185 define /health/deps endpoint. It returns a plain dict (no status_code parameter), so FastAPI defaults to HTTP 200 regardless of dependency health. Database, valkey, email, payments, error_tracking, and circuit_breakers statuses are reported but do not affect the response code.
findings.notes: Contrast with /health/ready (lines 188-229) which correctly returns status_code=503 when blocking dependencies are unavailable. /health/deps does not fail closed.

findings.evidence: Lines 106-149 (/health) checks only database and valkey. Lines 152-185 (/health/deps) checks database, valkey, email, payments, error_tracking, and circuit_breakers. Neither endpoint references R2, r2_bucket, r2_endpoint_url, storage, or Cloudflare R2 health.
findings.notes: R2 is a critical production storage backend per TECHNOLOGY_STACK.md L-68 (Cloudflare R2 for media blobs, audit archives). Health endpoints should verify R2 reachability.

findings.evidence: Lines 59-63 show _error_handler is initialized eagerly at module load time via create_error_handler(settings.sentry_dsn, ...). It is not None until first exception. Lines 66-67 define get_error_handler() as a simple return of the pre-initialized _error_handler.
findings.counter_evidence: Original finding claimed _error_handler was None until first exception triggered get_error_handler(), and that sentry_sdk.init failure at error_handler.py:78-79 would silently disable error tracking. Current code initializes _error_handler eagerly at import time, eliminating the lazy-init race condition.
findings.notes: Error handler is now eagerly initialized. The lazy-init vulnerability described in the audit has been remediated.
